text: 1 INTRODUCTION 1.1 Background DocAI is designed to address the growing need for intelligent, secure, and context-aware document retrieval systems. In today’s digital era, information is one of the most valuable assets for organizations, institutions, and businesses. Whether it is a multinational enterprise or a small educational institution, the ability to store, manage, and retrieve knowledge effectively impacts decision-making, operational efficiency, and compliance. It is important to remember that documentation—ranging from policy guides, training manuals, SOPs, compliance policies, to research reports—represents the institutional memory of an organization. Yet, due to the size and complexity of such documents, retrieval becomes a major challenge. Traditional methods like keyword search (Ctrl+F), indexes, and bookmarks are still common but operate on a lexical basis, depending on exact word matches, which often leads to irrelevant or missed information. To understand this problem more deeply, consider that corporate HR teams, legal professionals, or academic administrators regularly need to answer complex, multilayered questions. For example, an HR query may require going through hundreds of pages of policy documents, while legal professionals might need to cross-reference internal SOPs, legal codes, and case law. In these cases, keyword search often fails to grasp the intent behind a question. The emergence of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed this landscape by enabling systems to understand semantic meaning. This allows users to ask questions in natural language and receive answers that are contextually appropriate, shifting from manual, inefficient methods to AI-powered question-answering systems that summarize, explain, or extract salient points from large volumes of text. To apply these advances, this project implements Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to accurately respond to queries from internal PDF documents. The system begins by preprocessing documents and breaking them into semantically coherent chunks. These chunks are then embedded using a sentence transformer model, allowing the system to numerically capture their meaning. The resulting vector embeddings are stored in a local vector database, which enables rapid and efficient retrieval of relevant information. This approach ensures that the system remains fully offline, aligning with privacy-first principles and avoiding the use of external cloud services. Analyzing the process further, when a user submits a question, the system performs a similarity search within the vector database to identify the most contextually relevant text chunks. These are then passed to a locally hosted large language model, which uses them as context to generate a grounded, precise answer. By using a local vector database and on-premise inference, the system addresses concerns of data privacy, especially for sectors

2 with strict compliance regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, or those bound by corporate NDAs. Evaluating the reliability of responses, the project integrates a multi-agent verification mechanism within the RAG pipeline. Multiple agents assess the retrieved content, verify the factual integrity, and cross-check the generated output before it is presented to the user. This minimizes hallucinations and maintains high consistency with the original source material, significantly improving the trustworthiness and accuracy of the system’s answers. Finally, to create a scalable and future-ready architecture, the project is built in a modular manner, allowing seamless integration with workflow tools such as n8n. This design ensures easy adaptability across various domains, including human resources, healthcare, education, and legal document analysis. By combining offline privacy, semantic understanding, and multi-agent validation, DocAI is positioned as a modern, intelligent, and reliable solution for document intelligence in the enterprise ecosystem. 1.2 Objectives • Develop a secure offline document intelligence platform : Enable querying of large internal documents without cloud use to prevent data leakage. • Implement advanced PDF parsing : Utilize PyMuPDF to extract text accurately, including complex layouts like tables and multi-columns. • Design a modular multi-agent RAG pipeline : Assign separate agents to perform chunking, ranking, generation, and verification tasks. • Add a ChunkAgent for semantic segmentation : Segment extracted text into context-rich chunks optimized for retrieval. • Integrate a local vector database : Store and search embeddings in ChromaDB for high-speed offline retrieval. • Generate high-quality embeddings : Apply sentence-transformers to capture semantic meaning beyond keywords. • Create a RankerAgent for precision retrieval : Retrieve and order the most relevant chunks for a query. • Use a local LLM for answer generation : Employ Mistral 7B via Ollama to generate context-aware, offline answers.

3 • Add a VerifierAgent for factual accuracy : Validate answers against sources and provide references. • Build an intuitive and responsive frontend : Develop using React + Tailwind for document upload and chat functionality. • Develop a modular backend with FastAPI : Implement separate routes for ingestion, queries, and agent control. • Ensure privacy and regulatory compliance : Process all data locally to align with GDPR, HIPAA, and security policies. 1.3 Purpose , Scope and Applicability 1.3.1 Purpose The primary purpose of this project is to create an intelligent question-answering system capable of extracting and delivering precise information from large internal PDF documents. It is designed to address the challenges faced by organizations that deal with vast amounts of unstructured text, enabling users to retrieve quick and accurate responses to complex queries without manually searching through files. A core focus is to ensure privacy and security by operating entirely offline. By hosting both the language model and the vector database locally, the system retains sensitive data within the organization’s infrastructure, making it ideal for privacycritical domains such as healthcare, legal services, human resources, and enterprise knowledge management. The project also aims to guarantee the reliability of responses through contextual accuracy and verification. A multi-agent approach is implemented to retrieve the most relevant document segments, verify the extracted information, and cross-check the generated answers, thereby reducing the risk of errors or hallucinations. Finally, the system is built with a modular architecture that enables easy scaling and future enhancements. This flexibility ensures that additional features—such as integration with visual workflow tools like n8n—can be implemented with minimal effort, allowing the solution to evolve alongside organizational needs. 1.3.2 Scope The scope of DocAI is to transform large, unstructured internal PDFs into an intelligent, context-aware, and privacy-preserving Q&A assistant. This solution is designed to not only provide direct, relevant answers to user queries but also to integrate advanced

4 verification mechanisms, perform offline processing, and support modular scalability to effectively serve a wide range of industries. • Automate PDF Chunking and Processing : Break down large internal PDF files into semantically coherent sections to enable accurate retrieval and query matching. • Ensure Fully Offline Operation : Protect data privacy and security by processing all queries and documents locally without relying on cloud servers. • Adapt to Domain-Agnostic Application : Support multiple industries such as healthcare, education, HR, legal, and enterprise knowledge management. • Deliver Contextually Accurate Responses : Retrieve and present answers based on semantic meaning instead of simple keyword matching. • Leverage Multi-Agent Collaboration : Employ specialized agents to perform chunking, ranking, generating, and verifying answers to enhance reliability. • Provide Source Verification and Citations : Ensure factual accuracy by linking responses to original document sections as references. • Design a Modular Architecture : Create a flexible system that enables seamless integration of new features and supports scaling to larger datasets. • Integrate with Vector Databases : Use local vector databases like ChromaDB to perform fast and accurate semantic search. • Handle Complex Queries : Support multi-part, multi-step, or deeply contextual questions that require logical reasoning. • Enable Future Automation Readiness : Support integration with visual workflow orchestration tools like n8n for automating processes. • Optimize for Limited-Connectivity Environments : Ensure functionality in areas where internet access is restricted or unavailable.

5 • Support Cross-Document Query Handling : Answer questions that require retrieving and merging information from multiple PDFs. • Develop a User-Friendly Interface : Provide a simple, intuitive interface accessible to both technical and non-technical users. • Scale for Enterprise Use : Manage thousands of documents and serve multiple departments simultaneously. 1.3.3 Applicability DocAI demonstrates strong applicability across multiple domains. In privacysensitive and data-intensive sectors, it enables organizations to instantly extract accurate answers from large internal PDF documents, thereby making information retrieval faster, safer, and more efficient. The ability to process queries offline, verify responses with source references, and adapt to various document types makes the system valuable for industries such as healthcare, legal services, human resources, and enterprise knowledge management. In the academic and development context, this project serves as a powerful example of how to design a real-world intelligent system from scratch. It applies theoretical concepts from natural language processing, information retrieval, multi-agent architectures, and vector database search—into a functional, domain-agnostic tool. Students, educators, and project reviewers can use this as a blueprint to integrate AIdriven solutions into practical, real-life scenarios while ensuring data security and transparency. The system also applies to research institutions and corporate environments that require instant access to critical knowledge while maintaining strict data privacy. By enabling offline operations, supporting modular upgrades, and integrating with workflow automation tools like n8n, DocAI contributes not just as an academic project but as a scalable foundation to build advanced, secure, and context-aware AI assistants across diverse professional settings.

6 SURVEY OF TECHNOLOGIES DocAI – Offline Multi-Agent RAG Pipeline for Internal Document Intelligence is designed to process and query large internal documents, including HR manuals, policy documents, and SOPs, entirely offline. The system identifies the need for secure, fast, and accurate document retrieval while preserving data privacy. It applies retrieval-augmented generation techniques to enhance efficiency and relevance in responses. A thorough survey of modern web, backend, AI, and storage technologies was conducted to evaluate their suitability for speed, modularity, and offline capability. This analysis involved comparing frameworks and tools to determine the most effective options. The resulting tech stack was chosen to ensure scalability, maintainability, and high performance in real- world use. 2.1 Frontend Technologies Before finalizing the frontend stack for DocAI, multiple modern frameworks and libraries were evaluated to ensure fast performance, a clean UI, and smooth integration with the backend. The chosen tools needed to work well in an offline environment, support modular development, and allow quick prototyping. • React + Next.js: A component-based framework with optional server-side rendering (SSR) and built-in routing, which can also be packaged as a local Single Page Application (SPA). • Tailwind CSS: A utility-first CSS framework that enables rapid development of responsive, modern, and consistent UIs. • Axios: A lightweight HTTP client for making requests to FastAPI endpoints with ease. • Next.js Routing: Provides structured page navigation and layout management without extra configuration. Why React + Next.js? React with Next.js was chosen for its flexibility, speed, and developer-friendly architecture. It supports both SSR and static builds, making it easy to deploy offline for local demos. Since the team had prior experience with Next.js, development time was reduced. Combined with Tailwind CSS, the stack allows for quick creation of responsive interfaces, and Axios ensures smooth communication with the backend APIs. 2.2 Backend Technologies The backend technologies implement a high-performance, privacy-preserving architecture using Python 3.10+, FastAPI, and Uvicorn to process and serve AI-driven document intelligence. These tools integrate seamlessly to validate, manage, and

7 optimize data flows, enabling the system to deliver accurate and efficient query responses in an offline environment. • Core Backend (Python 3.10+) — Primary backend language with a rich ecosystem for AI/NLP and rapid prototyping. • FastAPI — High-performance Python web framework to expose REST endpoints for document upload, indexing, and question answering. • Uvicorn (uvicorn[standard]) — ASGI server that runs the FastAPI app with efficient async I/O. • Pydantic v2 — Data validation and typed request/response schemas for clean, reliable APIs. • python-dotenv — Loads configuration (paths, model names) from a .env file to keep code organized. • (Optional) loguru — Structured logging for easier debugging and error tracing. Why this combo? This stack is lightweight, fast, and well-suited for building privacy-preserving, offline microservices. FastAPI offers speed and developer productivity, while Python’s AI/NLP libraries integrate seamlessly for the RAG pipeline. 2.3 LLM & Retrieval Technologies Before finalizing the LLM and retrieval stack for DocAI, several offline-capable tools and frameworks were identified, evaluated, and selected to ensure privacy, high accuracy, and smooth integration with the backend. The chosen tools had to function without an internet connection, support semantic search, and allow easy deployment on typical hardware. • Ollama: Utilize to run the language model locally without internet connectivity. • Mistral 7B: Adopt for balancing quality and speed on standard systems. • Sentence-Transformers: Implement to generate embeddings locally for semantic search. • all-MiniLM-L6-v2: Apply as the embedding model to produce fast, 384- dimensional vectors. • ChromaDB (with persist_directory): Store and retrieve chunk embeddings with metadata in a local vector store. • LangChain (core/light use): Construct a simple RAG chain (prompts + retrieval) without heavy agent frameworks. Why these? These tools maintain the entire RAG pipeline fully offline, ensure privacy, and enable a lightweight, persistent, and easy-to-operate setup.

8 2.4 Multi-Agent Orchestration (V1) To coordinate the various stages of retrieval-augmented generation, a minimal multi- agent architecture was designed, implemented, and optimized for simplicity and debugging ease. • ChunkAgent: Parse documents, segment them into chunks, and generate embeddings. • RankerAgent: Retrieve the top-k relevant chunks from Chroma. • GeneratorAgent: Invoke the local LLM (via Ollama) to draft answers. • VerifierAgent: Validate that answers are grounded in retrieved chunks, add citations, or flag uncertainty. • Simple Orchestrator: Sequence calls to these agents for streamlined execution. Why this (and not heavy “Agents” libraries)? This approach establishes a clear multi-agent workflow, avoids unnecessary complexity, and facilitates easier debugging and explanation in V1. 2.5 File Processing & Parsing High-quality document parsing was prioritized, selected, and implemented to ensure accurate embeddings and reliable retrieval. • PyMuPDF (fitz): Utilize as the primary tool for PDF extraction to handle complex layouts more effectively than PyPDF2. • python-docx / docx2txt: Integrate optional support for processing .docx files. • pandas: Apply optionally for parsing and structuring tables. Why PyMuPDF? It delivers superior text fidelity for PDFs, minimizes artifacts, and ensures consistent results across enterprise and academic documents. 2.6 Storage & Data Handling A combination of relational and vector databases was selected, implemented, and maintained to ensure separation of concerns and portability. • SQLite: Store document metadata, session history, and application settings. • ChromaDB: Manage embeddings and chunk metadata for efficient retrieval. • Pydantic Settings + .env: Adopt as a safer method for configuring application parameters. • Local Filesystem: Preserve uploaded PDFs and processed artifacts.

9 Why SQLite + Chroma? SQLite handles application metadata, while Chroma specializes in vector search — both operate offline and remain lightweight. 2.7 Authentication (V1 Scope) For the initial offline demo, authentication was kept minimal. • None: Single-user, fully offline operation. • (Optional) Local JWT: If authentication becomes necessary, without requiring internet. Why? Avoids OAuth or cloud-based auth systems to preserve the core USP of complete offline privacy.
